status: fixed before calibration and real fitting
hypothesis: One raw EVA character maps to one Latin alphabet letter, many-to-one allowed. Base table everywhere except first character of a known token after a known token ending in EVA y within same line; then separate table. No semantic interpretation assigned.
controls: Latin Pliny and Italian Paradiso, two random bijective contextual encryption keys each; trigger y forced to base encoding of most frequent plaintext word-final letter in training prefix, alternative independent random permutation. No plaintext/key passed to optimizer.

calibration_gate.failure_policy: Stop real application; document failure and investigate separately without treating real negative result as exclusion.

split: Physical leaves sorted in union of four Voynich cases; every fifth starting index zero reserved test; all other leaves training pool. Prefix of full lines up to 24000 known characters. Test never used to select keys. Same split ZL/IT.
null: 19 deterministic shuffles per primary case; permute known interior word slots within each line, leave first/last slots and None barriers fixed; do not change line or whole-word inventory; shuffle train/test separately and refit both models. Weak null, does not preserve boundary relationships.
score: Heldout average negative log2 training-LM quadgram probability on common known-output windows between two models. Improvement = blind bits minus contextual bits. More positive is better. This is a language-model diagnostic, not translation accuracy on Voynich.
uncertainty: Commas, alternatives and unreadable groups remain None barriers, no changes to transcription. No line boundaries crossed. Raw EVA characters only.
comparison: No p-value claimed from 19 null fits; report full range and count of null gains as large as observed. No parameter or language selection using heldout. All candidates are NOT translations.
success_for_real: Never declare decryption from LM score; require stable recoverable key, linguistically coherent heldout text, independent validation; these tests alone insufficient.
